subtitle: std::expected<T,E> — C++23's discriminated-union 'value or error' wrapper. restd back-ports to C++11 (runtime correctness) with constexpr promoted to C++20, where placement-new becomes constexpr-accessible. Ships the full surface: expected<T,E> + expected<void,E> partial specialisation, unexpected<E> wrapper, bad_expected_access exception family (with three inheritance fallbacks: std::bad_cast / std::exception / standalone), unexpect_t tag, five operator== overloads (expected/expected, expected/value, expected/unexpected, void variants, unexpected/unexpected), non-member swap, the C++17 unexpected deduction guide. Monadic operations (and_then, or_else, transform, transform_error) ship in three ref-qualified overloads each, implemented via direct call syntax — function objects, lambdas, free function pointers all work; pointer-to-member-function does NOT (would require restd::invoke, blocked on <functional>). Reference specialisation expected<T&, E> deferred. Conditional triviality not implemented — restd always emits user-defined special members (correctness over optimisation, documented limitation).
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++23 <expected> header. Shipped on C++11+ (no C++98 path — the design requires variadic templates, rvalue refs, defaulted/deleted special members, and union-with-non-trivial-members, all C++11+ features). Constexpr from C++20 (ahead of std's C++23).

symbols.name: expected<T,E>
symbols.notes: Primary template. Anonymous union { T m_val; E m_err; } plus bool m_has_value discriminant; user-provided union ctor/dtor (mandatory when members aren't trivially destructible). Ten ctor flavours: default (value-inits T), copy, move, forwarding-from-U (gated to avoid hijacking copy/move/tag overloads), unexpected copy/move, in_place + in_place-with-initializer_list, unexpect + unexpect-with-initializer_list. Full assignment + emplace + member swap. Observers: has_value, operator bool, operator*, operator->, value (throws bad_expected_access<E> on failure), error, value_or. Monadic and_then/or_else/transform/transform_error each in three ref-qualified overloads (& / const & / &&). RESTD AHEAD OF STD: ships from C++11 (std waited for C++23 — 12-year back-port). Constexpr from C++20 (std's first constexpr was C++23 — 3-year lead).
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — implementation requires variadic templates, rvalue references, defaulted/deleted special members, and union-with-non-trivial-members, all C++11+ language features. C++98 aggregate-init won't apply because expected has user-declared ctors and private storage by design (discriminated union demands managed lifetime).

symbols.name: expected<void,E>
symbols.notes: Partial specialisation for void value type. Single-member union of just _E (with a char m_dummy placeholder for the success state). emplace() takes no args; in_place ctor takes no args; operator* is no-op; value() throws when !has_value but returns nothing on success. Monadic and_then/transform's callable takes no args (the unit type produces no payload to forward). Same constexpr tier as the primary template.
symbols.failure_reason: Same as expected<T,E> — C++11+ language features (variadic templates, rvalue refs, defaulted special members, union-with-non-trivial-members).

symbols.name: unexpected<E>
symbols.notes: Wrapper around an error of type _E. Three ctors: forwarding-from-Err (gated to avoid the copy/move/in_place overloads), in_place + args, in_place + initializer_list + args. Four ref-qualified error() accessors (& / const & / && / const &&). Member swap. C++17 deduction guide allows `unexpected u(err)` to deduce unexpected<decltype(err)>. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 12-year back-port from C++11; constexpr from C++20 (3-year lead vs std's C++23).
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — requires variadic templates, rvalue references, defaulted/deleted special members, all C++11+ features.

symbols.name: bad_expected_access<void>
symbols.notes: Base class for the bad_expected_access family. Three inheritance fallbacks (same scheme as bad_any_cast): inherits std::bad_cast when <typeinfo> available, falls back to std::exception when only <exception> available, standalone class otherwise. Protected ctor/dtor — only catchable via reference. Virtual what() returns 'bad expected access'. User code catches bad_expected_access<void>& to handle any expected access failure regardless of E.
symbols.failure_reason: Uses ref-qualified accessors (C++11 feature) and constexpr ctors. Gated on C++11+ for consistency with the rest of the module; would otherwise need a parallel C++98 path with less elegant member functions, which would be unused (the rest of <expected> is unavailable on C++98 anyway).

symbols.name: bad_expected_access<E>
symbols.notes: Templated payload-carrying exception. Inherits bad_expected_access<void>. Carries a copy of the unexpected error value; four ref-qualified error() accessors (& / const & / && / const &&). Thrown by expected<T,E>::value() when !has_value() — only when D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_EXCEPTION; degrades to a touch-and-return no-op (UB) otherwise, matching libstdc++ -fno-exceptions behaviour.
symbols.failure_reason: Same gate as bad_expected_access<void> — C++11 baseline for the whole module.

symbols.name: unexpect_t / unexpect
symbols.notes: Empty struct with explicit constexpr default ctor — the standard's defensive design (prevents accidental implicit construction from {} in contexts where a default-constructible parameter is also valid). The named instance `unexpect` is `inline constexpr` on C++17+; on C++11–C++14 falls back to a holder-template pattern (template static const member, address-of-safe under ODR because the type is empty).
symbols.failure_reason: Requires constexpr ctor (C++11 feature) for inline-constexpr-variable use. Gated on C++11+ for consistency with the module; the tag is meaningless without expected which is itself C++11+.

symbols.name: operator== (expected, expected)
symbols.notes: Cross-type comparison: expected<T1,E1> vs expected<T2,E2>. Equal iff both have-value matches AND (when has-value, *lhs == *rhs; when both have errors, lhs.error() == rhs.error()). Also provided as a separate overload for expected<void,E1> vs expected<void,E2> — has_value parity is the equality predicate, error compared lexically when both errored. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: ships on C++11+; constexpr from C++20.
symbols.failure_reason: Pre-C++11 lacks the language features (rvalue refs, etc.) that the expected class itself depends on. Comparison can't ship without the class.

symbols.name: operator== (expected, T)
symbols.notes: Compare an expected directly against a bare value. True iff expected has-value AND *expected == bare-value. Convenience: `if (e == 42)` reads more naturally than `if (e && *e == 42)`. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 12-year back-port.
symbols.failure_reason: Same as the rest of <expected>'s comparison family — depends on the expected class itself.

symbols.name: operator== (expected, unexpected)
symbols.notes: Compare an expected against a bare unexpected wrapper. True iff expected has no value AND lhs.error() == rhs.error(). Also ships for expected<void, E> vs unexpected<G>. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 12-year back-port.
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on the expected class itself which is C++11+.

symbols.name: operator== (unexpected, unexpected)
symbols.notes: Two unexpecteds compare equal iff their stored errors compare equal (defers to E's own operator==). Cross-type unexpected<E1> vs unexpected<E2> permitted when the cross-type op== exists. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 12-year back-port.
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on unexpected itself which is C++11+ (variadic ctors, rvalue refs).

symbols.name: operator!= (all variants)
symbols.notes: Explicit operator!= overloads for every operator== flavour (expected/expected, expected/T, expected/unexpected, unexpected/unexpected, plus void variants). Gated on `#if !D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP20_OR_HIGHER` — C++20's rewriting rules synthesise these from operator==, so explicit ones would create ambiguous overloads. The explicit versions are the only way to call != on C++11–C++17.
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on the expected class itself which is C++11+.

symbols.name: swap (expected)
symbols.notes: ADL-friendly non-member swap delegating to expected's member swap. Two overloads: expected<T,E> and expected<void,E>. The member swap handles all four (has-value, no-value) × (has-value, no-value) combinations, using ADL swap for same-state pairs and a placement-new dance for mixed-state pairs. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: ships on C++11+; constexpr from C++20.
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on the expected class itself.

symbols.name: swap (unexpected)
symbols.notes: ADL-friendly non-member swap delegating to unexpected's member swap (which swaps the stored error via ADL swap). Unconditionally noexcept.
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on unexpected itself which is C++11+.

symbols.name: unexpected deduction guide
symbols.notes: `unexpected(E) -> unexpected<E>` — enables `unexpected u(err)` to deduce the wrapper's template parameter from the argument. Gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP17_OR_HIGHER. CTAD is a C++17 language feature.
symbols.failure_reason: CTAD (class template argument deduction) is a C++17 language feature; cannot be back-ported to C++11–C++14. Users on those tiers must specify the template argument: unexpected<std::string>("err").
